A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RECON. All 19 pages of v1 and 26 pages of v2, including appendices A–C and A–G respectively, provide readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original symmetry-recovery experiments on MNIST, FashionMNIST and GEOM-QM9, neighborhood sensitivity analyses, and OOD pose-detection results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds centroid simulations, molecular-neighborhood validation, OOD comparisons and test-time classification experiments.

M1.justification: The IE-AE backbone, neighbor-based normalization and learned predictors remain intact. V2 adds an optional Tukey-Fréchet centroid using a bounded biweight loss for multimodal distributions, a focused extension of the centering step (Section 3.1; Appendix C). It also corrects the written canonicalization transform from psi Lambda^-1 to Lambda psi^-1; this does not establish that the earlier implementation used the incorrect expression.

E1.justification: The three named benchmarks are retained, but v2 adds classification under rotated inputs using frozen classifiers and test-time canonicalization (Appendix F.2). It also evaluates centroid estimation on sampled unimodal, bimodal, five-modal and uniform SO(2) distributions (Figure 8). These introduce a substantial new task and additional distribution scenarios.

E2.justification: V1 reports RECON-only OOD scores; v2 adds an uncentered IE-AE comparator in all three OOD experiments (Figures 5c and 13). New classification comparisons evaluate no canonicalization, IE-AE canonicalization and RECON (Figure 6d). The earlier SGM/IE-AE qualitative canonicalization comparison is retained, rather than newly introduced.

E3.justification: Appendix F.2 introduces classifiers trained without rotation augmentation and held fixed during evaluation on rotated inputs, with three preprocessing conditions and an unaugmented reference evaluation. Training uses 100 epochs for ResNet-18 and 50 for the GCN. Appendix C adds simulations with 2,000 samples per distribution. Existing IE-AE training budgets and GEOM splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds simulations testing centroid behavior around separated modes, a molecular-neighborhood purity analysis and its relationship to conformer counts, and an OOD ablation of centering (Appendices C, D.3 and F.1). The original neighborhood-size sensitivity and molecular-error correlation analyses survive as Appendix D.1 and Figure 12; their relocation is not new evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments use a fixed random seed and retain prediction error bars, neighborhood mean/standard-deviation bands and molecular standard-deviation plots. V2 introduces no repeated-seed evaluation, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure. Its additional descriptive statistics and result rows do not change the uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figure 6d adds RECON classification accuracies of 92.94%, 80.32% and 55.70%, versus 66.90%, 57.52% and 52.40% without canonicalization, for MNIST, FashionMNIST and GEOM-QM9 respectively. Figure 10 adds a mean neighborhood hit rate of 0.95. Reported OOD AUCs change from 0.92/0.80/0.75 in v1 Section 5.3 to 0.92/0.81/0.80 in v2 Figure 5c. V1's sparse OOD protocol description prevents interpreting these revisions as established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The original Wasserstein-consistency proposition and proof are largely retained. V2 adds Proposition B.2 and its proof concerning right-translation invariance of the likelihood score under a right Haar measure. Appendix C introduces population and empirical Tukey-Fréchet objectives and derives the loss gradient. The original consistency theorem is not extended to prove the robust variant's guarantees.

C1.justification: The symmetry-discovery, canonical-normalization and first-3D-demonstration claims remain. V2 substantially broadens the abstract, introduction and concluding contribution statements to claim inference-only canonicalization that grants group invariance to frozen pretrained models and improves downstream performance without retraining those models.

C2.justification: V2 recognizes problematic multimodal centroids and attributes OOD improvements to easier optimization despite theoretical reference-frame invariance of likelihood. Its limitations emphasize whole-input transformations versus object-local symmetries in cluttered scenes, and dataset bias in learned natural poses. V1 instead concentrates on molecular prediction errors, density families, sampling and predefined groups.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds substantial reproducibility information: OOD score formulas, GEOM ID/OOD construction and threshold 96, classifier architectures and training settings, and recomputation of geometric features after canonicalization. Appendix C documents robust-centroid optimization. Core implementation details largely move from v1 Appendix C to v2 Appendix E unchanged. Code-release wording changes to availability upon publication, while both PDFs still provide placeholder repository links.

R1.justification: V2 adds robust-statistics references by Shevlyakov et al., Rousseeuw and Hubert, and Shin and Oh. It also positions inference-only canonicalization against frame averaging and learned canonicalization, citing Puny et al. and Kaba et al. The central related-work discussion and positioning relative to SGM and IE-AE remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract, introduction and limitations around the broader canonicalization application. Experiments change from separate imaging, geometric-graph and OOD sections to symmetry recovery and downstream applications. Longer neighborhood and partial-symmetry discussions move into Appendix D, and the appendices are reorganized into dedicated theory, analysis, implementation and application sections.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned and moved to the first page with a new train/test distribution-shift illustration. The centroid illustration gains an additional distribution and estimator. New accuracy tables, centroid simulations, neighborhood-quality plots and ROC curves are introduced. Existing density plots, neighborhood sensitivity and molecular-error correlations move into appendices, substantially reorganizing the displays without deleting those results.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for normalization's practical value through frozen-classifier comparisons and an uncentered OOD control, addressing gaps in v1's qualitative canonicalizations and standalone OOD scores. Direct neighborhood validation supports a central sampling assumption, while the added likelihood-invariance proof and application details clarify mathematical scope and reproducibility. These are substantial gains, although the robust centroid extension has only simulation validation and fixed-seed reporting still limits confidence in experimental stability.
